prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Dallas for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on your needs (complexity, budget, insurance, aesthetic goals). I can help find top options near you — but first a few quick questions so I give useful recommendations:

- Do you mean Dallas, TX (city) or the Dallas–Fort Worth area? ZIP or neighborhood helps.  
- Is this a single implant or full-arch/replacement of many teeth?  
- Do you prefer a specialist (oral surgeon or periodontist) or a general dentist who does implants?  
- Do you have dental insurance or a timeline/budget?

Until you tell me, here’s how to identify the best implant provider and what to ask at consults:

Who to consider
- For implants, the most experienced clinicians are usually:
  - Oral and maxillofacial surgeons (complex surgery, bone grafts, extractions, sedation)
  - Periodontists (gum and bone management around implants)
  - Prosthodontists (best for the final restorative aesthetics and bite)
  - Some general dentists with extensive implant training also do excellent work for routine cases
- Ideally your team includes both a surgeon (or periodontist) and a prosthodontist if your case is complex.

How to verify skill and reputation
- Look for board certification or fellowship training (ABOMS for surgeons, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics, AAID membership). “Diplomate” status is a strong indicator.
- Ask how many implants they place per year and for cases like yours.
- Check patient reviews and before/after photos (Google, Yelp, Healthgrades, RealSelf). Also check professional directories: AAOMS, AAID, ADA find-a-dentist.
- Ask for referrals from your general dentist.

Questions to ask at consult
- How many implants like mine have you placed? What is your success rate?
- Will you take a CBCT 3D scan and use digital planning/guided surgery?
- Who will make my crown/bridge — you or a prosthodontist? Can I see examples?
- What implant system do you use and why?
- Will I need bone grafting or sinus lift? If so, how often do you do those?
- What anesthesia/sedation options do you offer?
- What is the full cost (surgery, implant, abutment, crown), payment plans, and expected timeline?
- What is your complication policy and warranty for restorations?

Red flags
- Provider unwilling to show cases or discuss experience
- Low or no use of 3D imaging for surgical planning on anything but trivial cases
- Vague cost estimates or refusal to provide a written treatment plan
- Pushy sales tactics for unnecessary add-ons

If you want, tell me your ZIP or neighborhood in Dallas and whether it’s a single implant or full-arch, and I’ll suggest several highly rated specialists/clinics and resources to check.
